Kenya · Contact

Request a proposal for wayleave mapping in Kenya

Tell us about the wayleave, reserve or site and what the record is for. We reply by email, in English, with the questions we need answered, and then with a written proposal covering the scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

About you
About the route or site

What do you need?

Location or province, the buffer distances to check, and any date the record must reflect.

Your request reaches us through FormSubmit, a form-delivery service. Read the privacy notice.

What happens next

  1. We reply by email to confirm what we need from you.
  2. A short scoping call about the route or site, the distances that matter and the imagery.
  3. A written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

What to send

The route or boundary file (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), the country and province, the distances to check, the date the record must reflect, the deliverables you need and your deadline. No file yet? Describe the location and we can draw the route with you.

Procurement teams

Send your supplier or prequalification forms, or the tender documents, with your request. The proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged.

For a wayleave or site in Kenya

  • The route or site file: KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage, or the wayleave or reserve polygons from your GIS.
  • The county or counties it crosses, so we can check the imagery that exists for the area.
  • The width to report: from the gazette order, easement, wayleave agreement or resettlement action plan, for example 30 m or 40 m for a transmission line, or the road or railway reserve.
  • Satellite only, or drone detail too. Drone work needs a Kenyan operator certificate, security clearances, KCAA authorisation of the operation and a month’s notice to the Director of Surveys, so the proposal shows the lead time. See drone law in Kenya.
  • The deadline, and any notice-of-intention, Gazette or cut-off date the record must reflect.
  • Who should receive the results, so they go only to the contacts you name.
  • The report language: reports are in English.

Frequently asked questions

Do you need a site visit or a drone flight to start?

No. A register starts from your route or boundary file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or imagery you already hold, so no one travels and no aircraft flies. Drone detail is added only where a stretch needs it, flown by a Kenyan company with a KCAA RPAS Operator Certificate and subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires.

We have no route file yet. Can we still ask?

Yes. Describe the line or pipeline and the counties and sub-counties it crosses, or send tower, kilometre-post or beacon coordinates, and we draw the route with you and send it back for your confirmation before any work runs.

Which date should the record reflect?

The one your process turns on, such as a notice of intention, a Gazette notice, a resettlement cut-off date or the date of an earlier scan. Tell us in the request, and the proposal says which dated imagery exists close to it before you commit.

Can we send tender or prequalification documents?

Yes. Send the documents with your request, and tell us the portal and the tender reference your process uses. Our procurement notes set out what applies to this kind of work in Kenya.

Our route crosses an area where travel advice warns against travel. Can you still help?

Yes, from satellite imagery. In the areas where government travel advice warns against travel, including Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, Lamu mainland, Tana River and West Pokot, the work is satellite only, with no one on the ground and no drone flight.
